title: POC Rapid Experiment Framework: model scaling & token efficiency
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working framework for rapid POC experimentation when the ask is: preserve user-perceived fidelity while minimizing token/compute cost and meeting 95th percentile latency targets. A set of heuristics and workflows for model selection, quantization trials, and prompt/pipeline tuning that SEs can run in a 2–4 week engagement.

Audience:
- Solutions engineers leading POC with customer technical teams
- Customer ML/infra partner who needs reproducible experiment plan

Goals (top-level):
1) Produce a small candidate matrix (3 models × 3 quant levels × 3 pipeline configs) to benchmark within 10–14 days.
2) Identify a safe rolling configuration for Dedicated/Private with fallbacks to hosted API.
3) Quantify cost vs. fidelity in terms the product/finance team understands (cost-per-response @ p95 latency).

Quick summary of approach:
- Start with a conservative model and aggressive prompts to get baseline quality and latency.
- Run an "adaptive quant ladder" where we test 8-bit -> 6-bit -> 4-bit in staged steps, checking hard failure modes (hallucination, formatting loss).
- Parallel prompt-pipeline sweeps: prompt prefix simplification, instruction gradient (short -> verbose), and token-level response truncation + reissue.
- Use a small held-out eval set (20–40 queries representative of production) with human-in-the-loop scoring for top 10 responses.

Experiment matrix (canonical):
- Model candidates: 1) Llama2-13B (baseline open model), 2) Redwood-optim-7B (mobile/edge candidate), 3) Falcon-40B-lite (high-fidelity reference).
- Quant tiers: q8_0 (symmetric 8-bit), q6_dynamic (per-layer 6-bit), q4_mix (4-bit mixed-int with fp16 KV cache).
- Pipeline configs: A) single-stage generation (no rerank), B) generate+light-filter rerank (sparse scoring), C) cascade: small model draft -> large model refine (cost-aware).

Notes on novelty: adaptive quant ladder
- Don’t jump straight to q4_mix. For each model, run q8_0 first, measure 1) exact-match for structured outputs, 2) semantic similarity (embedding cosine) vs baseline, 3) token generation anomalies.
- If q8_0 shows <1% structured output distortion and <3% embedding drift, step down to q6_dynamic. Repeat checks. Only move to q4_mix for model+task pairs where loss in human-judged utility is below threshold (typically 5–7% drop).

Prompt/pipeline heuristics to try early:
- Prefix compression: compress long system instructions into short canonical tokens and attach a small context decoder that expands the canonical tokens server-side. This reduces prompt token count for repeat requests.
- instruction-gradient: generate responses with 3 instruction verbosity levels in parallel; prefer the shortest response that passes downstream QA checks.
- response-slicing: for very long outputs, emit in segments using KV cache aware reissues to keep per-token latency low and allow early consumption by client.

Cache & batch heuristics:
- Prefix caching: cache first 128 tokens of common prompts (customer support templates). Warm cache during scheduled bursts.
- Dynamic batch headroom: aim for batch utilization 70–85% target; auto-throttle based on 95th percentile latency trend. If p95 > target, reduce batch batch-size by 1 step and increase parallelism.

Evaluation metrics (practical):
- Latency: p50/p95 token latency and end-to-end response time (ms) on target infra (dedicated GPU type).
- Cost: compute-cost per response (estimated $/response for Dedicated and hosted).
- Quality: human-rated utility (0-5), grammar-fluency (automated), and semantic-similarity (embedding cos to baseline).
- Failure taxonomy: hallucination rate (critical factual errors), output truncation errors, JSON/schema validity.

Runbook (two-week timeline):
Week 0 (prep): collect eval set, identify SLOs, provision test infra (small Dedicated pool or tiny private cluster), create baseline prompt templates.
Week 1 (sweep): run model × q8_0 × all pipelines with automated metrics and small human review of top 30 responses. Log regressions.
Week 2 (refine): for promising pairs, step the adaptive quant ladder (q6, then q4 if safe). Run cascade configs and measure cost delta. Produce decision memo and recommended config for canary.

Decision gates (accept/reject):
- Accept candidate if: p95 latency <= target AND human-utility >= baseline * 0.95 AND cost saving >= 20% vs baseline.
- Soft-accept (requires A/B in prod): utility 0.9–0.95 baseline but cost saving > 30% — requires canary and feature flag.
- Reject if hallucination > baseline * 1.1 or structured output failure > 1%.

Deployment recommendations by mode:
- Hosted API: prefer cascade (small draft + hosted refine) to reduce cost but keep fidelity. Use token-level meters and short-circuit rerank when cost spike detected.
- Dedicated: choose q6_dynamic unless metrics show no meaningful loss; set autoscale burst policy to allow fallback to hosted for traffic spikes.
- Private: be conservative — require passing q8_0 + q6_dynamic with audit logs enabled and HSM-stored model keys if required.

Safety and regression monitoring:
- Track prompt-set regressions: each rollout must run a small smoke eval (10 critical prompts) comparing current model+quant to previous production.
- Configure alerts for sudden drop in embedding similarity on sample streams (threshold 0.15 cosine drop).

Sample prompt templates (task: multi-turn summarization + action extraction)
- System: "You are a concise assistant that outputs JSON with keys: summary, actions[]. Keep summary <120 tokens."
- User-short: "Customer chat: [conversation]. Summarize and extract actions."
- Prompt-squeeze variant: remove polite boilerplate, rely on system instruction token to imply role. Compare quality delta.

Known risk cases and mitigations:
- Structured output drift under q4_mix: mitigation = keep fp16 KV cache and add schema-guard reranking (fast scorer that verifies JSON).
- Sensitive PII hallucination increase at lower quant: add detect-and-redact prefilter and route uncertain cases to bigger model.
- Latency spike due to batch sizing on burst traffic: mitigation = burst-only single-request lanes with higher vCPU/low-batch path.

Open questions / experiment ideas:
- Can we run a hybrid cache where short common completions are served from a warmed small 1B distilled model and only long-form runs go to the big model? (pipeline cost vs transition latency tradeoff).
- Feasibility of server-side canonical token expansion for customers (security + UX implications).
- Automated human-in-the-loop sampling cadence — is weekly enough for moderately dynamic domains?

Immediate next steps (owner: Samira):
- Lock eval set with customer (target: 30 canonical queries + 20 long-form).
- Spin up test infra: small dedicated pool (2x A10 / 1x H100 depending on model).
- Create initial run job in GH actions for automated sweeps: link to PR template (see linked_artifacts).
- Book 1-hour sync with Elena and field SE on 2025-01-14 to align acceptance criteria.

Appendix: quick checklist for SE on first day of POC
- Confirm SLOs and cost target with customer (explicit $/month or % reduction).
- Collect schema examples and golden JSON for structured tasks.
- Establish human review panel and scoring rubrics (5-point scales).
- Set up experiment tracking: metric dashboard (latency, cost) and logging hooks to console.

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Try smaller embed-based reranker to reduce calls to big refiner; tune similarity threshold conservatively.
- Make sure to sample from tail queries (rare, long context) — they usually break quantized models first.
- Remember to add SLA language for canary fallback in proposal doc.
